mainTopic: Pounding and sorting food on יום טוב, and which gifts (food, grain, clothing, כלאים) may be sent on יום טוב
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about pounding grain on יום טוב. רבא explains that two ברייתות do not really disagree: a small mortar is allowed in בבל, but it was forbidden in ארץ ישראל, where careless servants might misuse a large one. The גמרא then tells how רב פפי would not eat porridge at מר שמואל's house, and gives two reasons for his refusal. Next, a משנה brings a dispute about sorting (בורר) legumes on יום טוב. בית שמאי, בית הלל, and רבן גמליאל each take a different view, and the גמרא explains the limits of each. A second משנה discusses which gifts may be sent on יום טוב: animals, wine, oil, flour, and legumes, while grain is disputed. The גמרא forbids sending gifts in a convoy of three people and explains how רבי שמעון finds a use for grain. A third משנה permits sending clothing, even garments with כלאים, and gives a general rule: whatever can be used on יום טוב may be sent. The גמרא then searches for a permitted use of a כלאים garment, rejecting bedding and then a curtain, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא resolves the contradiction: one ruling for us, one for them
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two ברייתות about pounding with a small mortar do not really argue. Each one speaks to a different place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult. This ruling is for us, and that ruling is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers an earlier contradiction between two ברייתות about pounding grain on יום טוב. He says each one was meant for a different community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that permits a small mortar is for the people of בבל, who do not have many servants. The ruling that forbids it is for the people of ארץ ישראל, who have many servants. Servants might use a big mortar and claim it was a small one, so in ארץ ישראל pounding was forbidden altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This ruling is for us (in בבל)
And that ruling is for them (in ארץ ישראל)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the law of יום טוב itself is different in the two places. The basic permission to pound with a small mortar is the same. It was simply restricted where servants might misuse it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that a place with careless servants needs a stricter fence, comes back right away in the story of מר שמואל's house.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
phrases.notes: Standard formula for resolving a contradiction

phrases.english: this is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: Us = בבל (few servants); them = ארץ ישראל (many servants)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between ברייתות raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different contexts (geographic and social): each source speaks to a different population
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about whether a small mortar is allowed on יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree in principle. The ban applies where servants make misuse likely.

steps.title: רב פפי refuses porridge at מר שמואל's house
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב פפי visited מר שמואל's house on יום טוב, was served porridge, and did not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי happened to come to the house of מר שמואל. They brought him porridge, and he did not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows someone acting on the concern about pounding grain on יום טוב. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Porridge (דייסא) is made from pounded grain. רב פפי held back from eating because he suspected the grain had been pounded that day in a forbidden way. The next steps will test whether that suspicion was justified.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, chanced to visit
Porridge made from pounded grain or groats

phrases.aramaic: רַב פַּפֵּי אִקְּלַע לְבֵי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: Rav Pappi happened to come to the house of Mar Shmuel.
They brought him porridge,
and he did not eat it.
phrases.notes: Concerned it was pounded on the Festival itself

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פַּפֵּי אִקְּלַע לְבֵי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life case connected to the topic of pounding grain on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפי would not eat porridge that might have been pounded in a forbidden way on יום טוב

steps.title: Maybe they used a small mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not eat? Maybe the grain was pounded with a small mortar, which is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they made it with a small mortar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפי's refusal. Pounding with a small mortar is allowed in בבל, so maybe the porridge was made the permitted way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on רבא's rule in Step 1, a small mortar is fine for people in בבל. So there seems to be no reason to suspect the porridge. The question pushes us to explain what made רב פפי suspicious.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it, they prepared it

phrases.english: But perhaps they made it with a small mortar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind רב פפי's refusal in Step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's refusal to eat the porridge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small mortar is permitted, so the porridge may have been made in a permitted way and there is no reason to refuse it

steps.title: It was ground too finely for a small mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רב פפי saw the grain was very finely ground, which a small mortar cannot do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he saw that it was ground very finely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in Step 3. The porridge was ground too well to have come from a small mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small mortar only crushes grain roughly. Fine grinding points to a large mortar, which is forbidden. So רב פפי had real evidence for his suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: Ground very finely, crushed a lot

phrases.english: Because he saw that it was ground very finely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual evidence from the food itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The porridge might have come from a permitted small mortar
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine grinding showed it came from a large mortar

steps.title: Maybe it was made before the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: maybe the grain was pounded the day before יום טוב, when it was fully allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they made it yesterday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge. Even if a large mortar was used, it may have been used before יום טוב began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grinding on ערב יום טוב is completely permitted. So the fine grinding alone does not prove anything forbidden happened. The גמרא needs another clue to justify רב פפי.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, meaning on ערב יום טוב

phrases.english: But perhaps they made it yesterday?
phrases.notes: On the eve of the Festival, when it is permitted

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after Step 4's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the porridge was made in a forbidden way
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A large mortar is fine if used before יום טוב, so fine grinding does not prove a violation

steps.title: The husks looked freshly pounded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רב פפי saw the husks were bright and fresh, so the grain had just been pounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he saw that its brightness was peeling, meaning it looked fresh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 5. The grain looked freshly pounded, so it must have been done on יום טוב itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain pounded a day earlier loses its fresh, bright look. The bright appearance showed it had been pounded that same day. Together with Step 4, this shows it was pounded on יום טוב with a large mortar.

keyTerms.meaning: Its brightness or shine (of the husks)

phrases.english: Because he saw that its husks were bright and freshly peeled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual evidence from the food itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The porridge may have been pounded on ערב יום טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: Its fresh look showed it was pounded on יום טוב itself

steps.title: Another answer: מר שמואל's house had careless servants
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: מר שמואל's house was different because it had servants who were careless. So even a small mortar should have been forbidden there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: מר שמואל's house is different, because there is carelessness among the servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reason for רב פפי's refusal, one that does not need the clues about the food. It ties the story back to רבא's rule in Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר שמואל had servants, and servants tend to be lax about rules. Just like in ארץ ישראל, a house with servants should forbid all pounding on יום טוב. So even small-mortar porridge was a concern there.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces an alternative answer

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רב פפי: (1) clues in the food showed it was pounded on יום טוב with a large mortar, or (2) a house with careless servants should not pound at all on יום טוב, as רבא said about ארץ ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer applies רבא's distinction to a single household. The reason for the strictness is the servants, not the location.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the house of Mar Shmuel is different,
because there is laxity among the servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the original question of Step 3, instead of relying on Steps 4 and 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies רבא's servant-based distinction to a specific household
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Small-mortar pounding is fine anywhere in בבל
steps.terutzMaskana: A house with careless servants falls under the stricter rule, like ארץ ישראל

steps.title: משנה: how one may separate legumes on the holiday
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. בית שמאי say one may only pick out food to eat right away. בית הלל allow normal selecting with ordinary vessels, but not with special sorting tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sorts legumes on יום טוב: בית שמאי say he picks out food and eats it. בית הלל say he sorts in his normal way, in his lap, in a basket, or in a dish, but not on a board, in a fine sieve, or in a coarse sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic: separating (בורר) legumes from waste on יום טוב. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about how much sorting is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow only picking out food to eat on the spot. בית הלל allow regular sorting as one normally does at home. בית הלל exclude special sorting tools, and the stricter בית שמאי surely forbid them too, because using them looks like weekday work.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates or sorts (food from waste)
Fine sieve and coarse sieve, special sorting tools

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: in this משנה, בית הלל are the more lenient side. They allow normal sorting, while בית שמאי allow only picking food to eat right away.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sorts legumes on a Festival,
Beit Shammai say:
he picks out food and eats it.
And Beit Hillel say:
he sorts in his usual way, in his lap,
in a basket-vessel or in a dish,
but not on a board,
nor with a fine sieve, nor with a coarse sieve.
phrases.notes: Special sorting tools look like weekday labor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: sort only to eat immediately. בית הלל: sort normally with household vessels, but not with dedicated sorting tools.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: one may even wash and skim
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל is even more lenient. One may put the legumes in water and skim off the waste that floats up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: He may even rinse them and skim off the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a third opinion. רבן גמליאל allows an even easier way of sorting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting legumes in water makes the waste float to the top so it can be skimmed off. רבן גמליאל permits this on יום טוב too. The word אף ("even") shows he goes beyond בית הלל's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Skims off, draws out (the floating waste)

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
he may even rinse and skim off.
phrases.notes: Waste floats in water and is removed

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, more lenient view to the dispute in Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל permits rinsing legumes in water and skimming off the floating waste on יום טוב

steps.title: בית הלל's leniency applies only when food is the majority
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן גמליאל: בית הלל allow removing the waste only when there is more food than waste. When the waste is more, everyone agrees you take out the food and leave the waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is taught in a ברייתא that רבן גמליאל said: When does this rule apply? When the food is more than the waste. But if the waste is more than the food, everyone agrees that one takes the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that limits when בית הלל allow normal selecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל allowed selecting in the usual way, which means picking out the waste. This ברייתא adds a condition: that only works when the food is the majority. If the waste is the majority, even בית הלל agree you must pick out the food instead.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limit on a rule)
Waste, refuse mixed in with the food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל allow removing waste in every case. This ברייתא limits their leniency to a mixture where most of it is food.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It is taught: Rabban Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
When the food is more than the waste,
but if the waste is more than the food,
everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאוֹכֵל וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַפְּסוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: one takes the food and leaves the waste.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 8 by limiting בית הלל's leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing the waste is allowed only when the food is the majority. When the waste is the majority, one must take the food out.

steps.title: Who would ever allow removing waste when most of the mixture is waste?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say 'everyone agrees' about a mixture that is mostly waste. Nobody would allow removing the waste in that case anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the waste is more than the food, is there anyone who would allow it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'everyone agrees' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'everyone agrees' suggests that someone might have thought otherwise. But when most of the mixture is waste, it is obvious that nobody would allow picking out all that waste. So why did the ברייתא need to say it?

phrases.english: If the waste is more than the food,
is there anyone who permits it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the phrase 'everyone agrees' from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'דברי הכל' in the ברייתא of רבן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case is so obvious that there is no reason to say everyone agrees about it.

steps.title: More waste means more effort, not more volume
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא means a case where the waste is smaller in amount but takes more work to remove. In that case, everyone agrees you take out the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the waste takes more effort to remove, even though it is smaller in amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing what 'more waste' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'the waste is more' means more effort, not more volume. Picture tiny pieces of waste scattered through mostly good food. Even though there is more food, removing the waste is harder, so even בית הלל agree you should pick out the food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows how much work is involved, not only how much there is. If removing the waste is more work, you take out the food instead.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where it is greater in effort
and smaller in amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דִּנְפִישׁ בְּטִרְחָא וְזוּטַר בְּשִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'More waste' seemed to mean a larger amount of waste, which would make 'everyone agrees' obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'More waste' means more effort to remove. Since that case is not obvious, the ברייתא needed to say that everyone agrees.

steps.title: How רבן גמליאל's household washed lentils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן גמליאל's line from the משנה and brings a ברייתא from רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. His household would fill a bucket with lentils and add water, so the food sank and the waste floated up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: One may even wash and skim off the waste. It is taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said: This was the custom of רבן גמליאל's household. They would bring a bucket full of lentils and pour water over it. The food ended up below and the waste above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבן גמליאל's words from the משנה and brings a ברייתא showing how his household actually did this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'wash and skim off.' The ברייתא shows the method: water separates the lentils from the waste by itself, so no picking by hand is needed. It also confirms that רבן גמליאל's household really followed this practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Pour water over so things float

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: One may even wash and skim off.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגָן שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: This was the custom of the house of Rabban Gamliel:
they would bring a bucket full of lentils
and pour water over it,
and the food was found below
and the waste above.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף מֵדִיחַ וְשׁוֹלֶה. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the משנה, רבן גמליאל's ruling from step 9, and illustrates it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lentils may be separated from their waste with water. The food sinks and the waste floats, so no hand-sorting is needed.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to another ברייתא that says the reverse: the food floated up and the waste sank down.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't the opposite taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two ברייתות about which part sinks and which part floats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says the food sank and the waste floated. Another ברייתא reports the reverse. Both cannot simply be right, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? (introduces a contradicting ברייתא)

phrases.english: But isn't the opposite taught?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the description in step 13 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the food sank and the waste floated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא describes the reverse result, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: It depends on whether the waste is dirt or straw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: one ברייתא is talking about dirt, which sinks, and the other about straw, which floats.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about dirt, and that one is about straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by explaining that each ברייתא is describing a different kind of waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heavy dirt sinks below the lentils, so in that case the food is on top. Light straw floats above the lentils, so in that case the food is below. Both ברייתות are correct, each for its own kind of waste.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)

steps.whatToRemember: Washing works either way. Whether the waste sinks or floats depends on what it is: dirt sinks and straw floats.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about dirt,
that one is about straw.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּעַפְרָא, הָא בְּגִילֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to describe the same situation with opposite results.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא describes a different kind of waste. Dirt sinks below the food, and straw floats above it.

steps.title: New משנה: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about sending gifts on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow sending only ready food portions on יום טוב. בית הלל also allow sending animals and birds, whether alive or slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: on יום טוב you may only send portions of food. בית הלל say: you may send domestic animals, wild animals, and birds, whether alive or slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what gifts you may send to someone on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי limit gifts to food that is already prepared and ready to eat. בית הלל are more lenient. They allow even live animals, since those can still be slaughtered and eaten on יום טוב. The underlying idea is that a gift is fine as long as it can serve a יום טוב need.

keyTerms.meaning: Domestic animal, wild animal, and bird

steps.confusionAlert: In this list, חַיָּה means a wild animal. But in the next phrase, חַיִּין means 'alive.' The two words look alike, but they mean different things.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא מָנוֹת,
phrases.english: One may send on Yom Tov only portions (of food),
And Beit Hillel say:
One may send domestic animals, wild animals, and birds,
whether alive or slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the discussion of sorting waste from food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי allow only food portions. בית הלל allow animals and birds, alive or slaughtered.

steps.title: Wine, oil, flour, and legumes may be sent, but grain is disputed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues, following בית הלל: one may send wine, oil, flour, and legumes, but not grain. רבי שמעון permits grain as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may send wines, oils, flours, and legumes, but not grain. רבי שמעון permits grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more items that may be sent, draws a line at grain, and then records that רבי שמעון disagrees about grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain is excluded because it normally has to be ground before it can be used, and grinding is not allowed on יום טוב. רבי שמעון holds that grain can still be used without grinding, so it may be sent. The גמרא will soon explain how.

phrases.english: One may send wines, oils, flours, and legumes,
but not grain.
And Rabbi Shimon permits grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more permitted items and one disputed item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine, oil, flour, and legumes may be sent. The תנא קמא forbids grain, but רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: רב יחיאל adds a condition: not in a convoy
steps.stepSummary: רב יחיאל teaches that sending gifts is allowed only if it is not done in a convoy (שורה) of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יחיאל taught: as long as he does not send it in a convoy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by adding a limit to the משנה's permission to send gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the item itself may be sent, a row of people carrying goods looks like merchandise being brought to market. That would look like weekday business and would make light of יום טוב. So the permission depends on how the gift is sent.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא: start of the גמרא section
Taught (introduces a teaching in the style of a ברייתא)
A row or convoy of people carrying items

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yechiel taught:
Provided that he does not do it in a convoy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the משנה's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gifts may be sent on יום טוב, but not in a convoy.

steps.title: A convoy means at least three people
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines a שורה: it is never fewer than three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a convoy is no fewer than three people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that defines the word שורה from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a number. One or two people carrying gifts is fine. Three or more people together count as a convoy and are not allowed.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוּרָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: A convoy is no fewer than three people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵין שׁוּרָה פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term שורה used by רב יחיאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three or more people count as a שורה.

steps.title: רב אשי asks about three people carrying three different foods
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if three people each carry a different kind of food, is that still a convoy?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: three men and three kinds of food, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question about where the edge of the convoy rule lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people normally make a שורה. But when each person carries something different, maybe it no longer looks like one shipment of goods going to market. Instead, it may look like three separate gifts. רב אשי asks which way we view it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question, a dilemma)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
Three men and three kinds (of food), what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the three-person definition with a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a שורה require the same kind of goods, or do three people count as a convoy no matter what each one carries?

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says תיקו: there is no answer, and the question stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב אשי's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to settle the case. So it remains a doubt whether three people with three different foods make a convoy.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Gifts may be sent on יום טוב, but not in a convoy of three or more people. Three people carrying three different foods is an unresolved case (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether three people with three different foods count as a שורה remains unresolved.

steps.title: How grain can be used on יום טוב according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains רבי שמעון's view: grain can be used without grinding. Wheat can be made into a dish, barley fed to animals, and lentils crushed into a dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי שמעון permits grain.' It was taught: רבי שמעון permits grain, for example, wheat to make לודיות from it, barley to put before his animal, and lentils to make רסיסין from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the last line of the משנה about sending gifts and brings a ברייתא showing how grain is useful on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbade sending grain because grain needs grinding. The ברייתא shows uses that need no grinding: wheat for a kind of food, barley as animal feed, and lentils crushed into a dish. Since grain has a real יום טוב use, רבי שמעון allows sending it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A food made from whole wheat (a type of cookie or porridge)

steps.confusionAlert: Lentils were already allowed in the משנה as legumes (קטניות). Here the ברייתא lists them as an example of how even raw, unprepared produce can be put to use on יום טוב.

phrases.english: 'Rabbi Shimon permits grain.'
It was taught: Rabbi Shimon permits grain,
for example: wheat, to make ludiyot from it,
barley, to put before his animal,
lentils, to make resisin from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the last clause of the משנה after the convoy discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון permits sending grain because it has יום טוב uses that do not require grinding.

steps.title: New משנה: clothing may be sent, even with כלאים
steps.stepSummary: One may send clothing, sewn or unsewn, even if it contains כלאים, as long as it serves a need of the festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may send clothes, sewn or unsewn, and even if they contain כלאים, as long as they are for the needs of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and moves from sending food to sending clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing is allowed because it can be used on יום טוב. The משנה even includes a garment with כלאים, which may not be worn, as long as it serves a festival need. What use such a garment could have on יום טוב is exactly what the גמרא asks starting in Step 26.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixture of wool and linen (שעטנז)
For the needs of the festival

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One may send clothes
whether sewn or not sewn,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כִּלְאַיִם
phrases.english: and even if they contain kilayim,
as long as they are for the needs of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that continues the theme of sending gifts, now applied to clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothing may be sent on יום טוב, even if it contains כלאים, when it serves a festival need.

steps.title: Shoes that may not be sent
steps.stepSummary: One may not send a spiked sandal or an unsewn shoe. רבי יהודה adds that a white shoe may not be sent either, since it needs a craftsman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But not a nailed sandal, and not an unsewn shoe. רבי יהודה says: not even a white shoe, because it needs a craftsman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists exceptions: footwear that cannot be used on יום טוב may not be sent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages forbade wearing a nailed sandal on שבת and יום טוב, so it has no יום טוב use. An unsewn shoe cannot be worn yet. רבי יהודה adds the white shoe, which people did not wear until a craftsman blackened it. So it too is useless on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with nails in it

phrases.english: But not a nailed sandal
and not a shoe that is not sewn.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not even a white shoe,
because it needs a craftsman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists exceptions to the permission to send clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nailed sandal and an unsewn shoe may not be sent. רבי יהודה also forbids a white shoe.

steps.title: The general rule: whatever can be used on יום טוב may be sent
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: anything you may benefit from on יום טוב, you may send.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything that one may use on יום טוב, one may send it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one simple rule that ties together all the cases above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case fits this one test. Food, animals, grain (according to רבי שמעון), and clothing are allowed because they can be used on יום טוב. The nailed sandal, the unsewn shoe, and the white shoe are forbidden because they cannot be used.
steps.whatToRemember: The test for sending a gift on יום טוב is simple: can the item be used on יום טוב? If yes, it may be sent. If no, it may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule gives one standard for every gift question. It explains the earlier disputes too: the argument over grain is about whether grain can be used on יום טוב.

phrases.english: This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב — מְשַׁלְּחִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: Anything one may use on Yom Tov, one may send it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the cases of the משנה into one principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Anything usable on יום טוב may be sent on יום טוב.

steps.title: What use is a garment of mixed wool and linen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lets one send כלאים garments on יום טוב, since one cannot wear them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense that sewn clothes may be sent, because they can be worn. Unsewn clothes can at least be used as a cover. But garments of כלאים: what are they good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה from Step 23. A כלאים garment seems to have no permitted use on יום טוב, so why may one send it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 25 is that you may only send what you can benefit from on יום טוב. Sewn and unsewn clothes pass that test. A כלאים garment is forbidden to wear, so it seems to fail the test.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; granted (introduces the easy cases before the hard one)
A forbidden mixture of wool and linen (שעטנז)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that sewn or unsewn clothes may be sent. The only problem is the כלאים case.

phrases.english: Gemara: It makes sense regarding sewn clothes:
they are fit for wearing.
Those that are not sewn, also:
they are fit for covering oneself.
But כלאים, what are they fit for?
phrases.notes: One may not wear them, so what is the יום טוב use?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's permission to send כלאים, using the rule from Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that כלאים garments may be sent on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sending is only allowed for items usable on יום טוב. כלאים cannot be worn, so it seems unusable.

steps.title: Suggestion: spread it underneath yourself
steps.stepSummary: A possible answer: the כלאים garment can be spread out and lain upon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that they are fit to spread underneath oneself,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible use for כלאים: lying on it instead of wearing it. The very next line will test this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse forbids כלאים 'upon you,' so lying on top of it might seem allowed. If that were so, the garment would be useful on יום טוב and could be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer that will be tested)

phrases.english: And if you will say they are fit to spread underneath oneself,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible use to answer Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposes a permitted use (lying on the garment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאים seems to have no use at all
steps.terutzMaskana: It could be used as a sheet to lie on

steps.title: The Sages forbade lying on כלאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that although the Torah allows lying on כלאים, the חכמים forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'Do not let it come upon you.' This means you may spread it beneath you. But the חכמים said it is forbidden to do so, in case a thread wraps around his skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 27 by quoting a ברייתא. The חכמים forbade lying on כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law only wearing it ('upon you') is forbidden, so lying on it would be allowed. The חכמים still forbade it out of worry that a loose thread could wrap onto the body, which would be like wearing it. So lying on it is not a permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a rejecting source)
'Do not let it come upon you' (ויקרא יט:יט)
To spread it out (as a sheet)

steps.confusionAlert: Lying on כלאים is allowed by Torah law. The prohibition comes from the חכמים, but that is still enough to reject the suggestion.

phrases.english: But it was taught: 'Do not let it come upon you.'
But you may spread it beneath you.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: However, the Sages said: It is forbidden to do so,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תִּכָּרֵךְ לוֹ נִימָא עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ.
phrases.english: in case a thread wraps itself on his skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'spread underneath' suggestion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects lying directly on כלאים as a permitted use
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים forbade it because a thread might wrap onto the body

steps.title: Suggestion: put something in between
steps.stepSummary: A new suggestion: use the כלאים underneath, with another layer separating it from the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that something separates in between,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix the problem from Step 28. Put another layer between the person and the כלאים, so no thread can touch his skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was a thread wrapping onto the body. A separating layer seems to remove that worry, so the כלאים could serve as padding underneath.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי,
phrases.english: And if you will say that something separates in between,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְסֵיק מִידֵּי בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the rejected suggestion to avoid the thread concern.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refines the case (adds a separating layer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lying on כלאים is forbidden because of loose threads
steps.terutzMaskana: With a separating layer the worry is gone, so it may be used underneath

steps.title: Even under ten mattresses it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A tradition from the holy community in ירושלים forbids sleeping on כלאים even with ten mattresses on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, in the name of רבי, in the name of the holy community in ירושלים: Even with ten mattresses one on top of the other and כלאים underneath them, it is forbidden to sleep on them, because it says 'Do not let it come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 29. Even with many layers in between, sleeping on top of כלאים is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than Step 28. The concern is not only a loose thread. Sleeping on top of כלאים at all is forbidden, no matter how many layers separate. So the separating layer does not create a permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he not say? (introduces a rejecting statement)
The holy community in Jerusalem (a respected group of sages)

phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that Rebbi said in the name of the holy community in Jerusalem:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עֶשֶׂר מַצָּעוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ
phrases.english: Even ten mattresses, one on top of the other,
with כלאים underneath them:
it is forbidden to sleep on them
(because it says: 'Do not let it come upon you').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'separating layer' suggestion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects any use of כלאים as bedding underneath a person, even with separation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Separation does not help; sleeping above כלאים is forbidden in any case

steps.title: Suggestion: use it as a curtain
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the כלאים cloth can be hung as a curtain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is fit for a curtain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the bedding idea and suggests a new use. The כלאים cloth can be hung up as a curtain, which is not worn or lain on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curtain hangs on the wall or in a doorway. It does not touch or cover the body, so it seems free of the כלאים prohibition. That would make it a real יום טוב use.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new answer after the earlier ones failed)
As a curtain / in the case of a curtain

phrases.english: Rather, it is fit for a curtain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bedding approach after it was rejected twice and proposes a curtain.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New use that avoids bodily contact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלאים has no permitted use at all
steps.terutzMaskana: It can be hung as a curtain

steps.title: People warm themselves with curtains
steps.stepSummary: עולא says a curtain can become טמא because a servant warms himself with it. So a curtain is also used on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But עולא said: Why did they say a curtain can become טמא? Because the servant warms himself with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the curtain answer with a statement of עולא. Curtains are in fact used on the body, so a כלאים curtain would also be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something hanging on a wall should not become טמא like a garment. עולא explains that it does, because a servant wraps himself in it to keep warm. That shows a curtain is treated like a body covering, so a כלאים curtain still runs into the prohibition. The question is still open here.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure; able to receive טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is talking about טומאה, not כלאים. The גמרא uses his reason to show that people use curtains on their bodies, and that is what causes the כלאים problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: All three suggested uses have now been rejected, so the original question from Step 26 is still standing.

phrases.english: But Ulla said:
Why did they say a curtain is impure (can become טמא)?
Because the attendant warms himself with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the curtain answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: People wrap themselves in curtains for warmth, so a כלאים curtain is also forbidden
